_metadata.description: WellaPath Nigeria CDSS — Full Top-50 Knowledge Base

Medical reviewer fix: hypertension severity_levels.severe populated
Medical reviewer fix: diabetes DKA symptoms added
Medical reviewer fix: rf_147 RTI bug corrected

demographic_modifiers.note: Highest mortality risk — fast-track evaluation required
Risk of severe malaria and maternal anaemia — escalate
Greater risk of rapid decompensation

seasonal_modifiers.note: Peak transmission May–October in Nigeria — higher match probability

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with malaria or another fever-causing condition. Malaria is a common and serious illness in Nigeria — prompt testing and care is strongly advised.

demographic_modifiers.note: Increase urgency if fever or feeding difficulty; watch for fast breathing
Consider secondary infection risk; escalate if symptoms worsen

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher incidence during Harmattan (Nov–Feb) due to dry dusty air

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a common cold or mild upper respiratory illness. Most cases resolve with rest and fluids, but seek care if your symptoms worsen or breathing becomes difficult.
conditions.care_level: Self-care / Pharmacy (Clinic if red flags or children with fever)

demographic_modifiers.note: Dehydration can be fatal rapidly in young children — escalate urgency
Severe acute malnutrition — emergency escalation regardless of primary condition severity
Moderate acute malnutrition — increase urgency by one tier
Monitor for dehydration closely — escalate faster than normal

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher incidence May–October through contaminated water and food

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with acute diarrhoea. Staying hydrated with oral rehydration solution (ORS) is important. Seek care promptly if you cannot drink fluids, feel very weak, or symptoms worsen.
conditions.duration_note: Sudden onset of frequent watery stools indicates acute diarrhoea. If stools have been watery for more than 3 days, or if dehydration signs appear, urgency increases significantly.

demographic_modifiers.note: Increase urgency — rapid dehydration risk
Severe acute malnutrition — emergency escalation regardless of primary condition severity
Moderate acute malnutrition — increase urgency by one tier

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher incidence; increase base weight

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with dysentery, a form of diarrhoea that can cause dehydration. Please seek medical care promptly — treatment and rehydration are important.
conditions.care_level: Clinic / Emergency (if severe dehydration or altered consciousness)

demographic_modifiers.note: Increase urgency — higher complication risk
Increase urgency

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher transmission via contaminated water

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with typhoid fever or another infection. Typhoid is treated with antibiotics — a clinic visit is recommended for testing and treatment.

demographic_modifiers.note: Highest mortality risk — immediate emergency referral
High mortality — immediate emergency referral
Increase urgency — maternal and fetal risk

seasonal_modifiers.note: Epidemic risk highest during rainy season and flooding events

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a severe dehydrating illness such as cholera. This is a medical emergency — seek care immediately and begin oral rehydration if available.
conditions.duration_note: Symptoms typically begin suddenly within hours of exposure; profuse watery stools may lead to life-threatening dehydration within 24 hours if untreated

demographic_modifiers.note: Escalate if breathing changes or high fever — risk of lower respiratory involvement
Escalate if fever or weakness; risk of secondary pneumonia

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher incidence during Harmattan (Nov–Feb)

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with an upper respiratory tract infection such as a cold or flu. Most cases resolve on their own, but seek care if symptoms worsen or breathing becomes difficult.

demographic_modifiers.note: Higher risk of severe disease; escalate sooner
Check breathing rate; escalate if fast breathing

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher incidence; dry air worsens symptoms

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a lower respiratory infection. Please see a healthcare provider — some respiratory infections require treatment and monitoring.

demographic_modifiers.note: Increase urgency — risk of rapid spread
Escalate if fever accompanies rash — exclude measles/mpox

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a skin infection or skin condition. Many skin conditions are treatable — a pharmacy or clinic visit is recommended for assessment.
conditions.care_level: Pharmacy / Clinic (Emergency if severe allergy or rapidly spreading infection)

demographic_modifiers.note: ESCALATE — UTI in pregnancy has high complication risk; treat promptly
Higher baseline prevalence
Risk of silent UTI progressing to sepsis; escalate with fever

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a urinary tract infection. This is usually treated with antibiotics — see a healthcare provider for assessment and treatment.

demographic_modifiers.note: Higher prevalence; escalate if weight loss or anaemia signs
Severe acute malnutrition — emergency escalation regardless of primary condition severity
Moderate acute malnutrition — increase urgency by one tier

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with an intestinal worm infestation. This is common and treatable — a pharmacist or clinic can recommend appropriate deworming treatment.
conditions.care_level: Pharmacy / Clinic (Clinic for children, persistent symptoms, or red flags)

demographic_modifiers.note: Neonatal eye discharge requires urgent assessment — risk of ophthalmia neonatorum

seasonal_modifiers.note: Dry dusty air increases conjunctivitis incidence

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with an eye infection. Most mild eye infections respond to treatment — see a pharmacist or clinic. Seek urgent care if your vision is affected or there is significant pain.
conditions.care_level: Pharmacy / Clinic (Emergency if injury, chemical exposure, or vision loss)

demographic_modifiers.note: Higher risk and can progress faster; escalate with high fever or feeding refusal

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with an ear infection. Most ear infections are treatable — please see a clinic, especially if fever is present or a child is affected. Seek emergency care if there is swelling behind the ear or severe headache.
conditions.care_level: Clinic (Emergency if mastoiditis signs or neurological symptoms)

demographic_modifiers.note: Increased risk of gum disease; routine dental care advised

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a dental or oral condition. Pain relief may help temporarily, but dental assessment is recommended. Seek emergency care if swelling spreads to the face or neck.
conditions.care_level: Pharmacy / Dental Clinic (Emergency if spreading swelling or airway risk)

demographic_modifiers.note: High dehydration risk; escalate faster
Higher risk of rapid dehydration

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher incidence through contaminated food/water

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with gastroenteritis. Staying hydrated is very important. If you cannot keep fluids down or feel very weak, seek medical attention promptly.

demographic_modifiers.note: Always escalate — multiple causes possible
Higher risk of missed serious cause
Escalate — fever in pregnancy has significant risk

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms include a fever that may need further investigation to identify the cause. Please see a healthcare provider — several conditions cause prolonged fever and testing can help identify the right treatment.

demographic_modifiers.note: Significantly increase urgency
Highest risk of complications
Severe acute malnutrition — emergency escalation regardless of primary condition severity
Moderate acute malnutrition — increase urgency by one tier

seasonal_modifiers.note: Epidemic peaks common January–April in Nigeria

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with measles or another rash-causing illness. Measles can be serious — please seek care promptly and avoid close contact with others to reduce spread.

demographic_modifiers.note: Vertical transmission risk; escalate and refer for specialist care
Higher risk of chronic disease

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a liver condition such as hepatitis. Yellowing of the eyes or skin with fatigue warrants prompt medical evaluation — please visit a clinic for assessment.

demographic_modifiers.note: Significantly increase urgency — TB/HIV co-infection very common in Nigeria
Increase urgency
Higher risk of atypical presentation

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with tuberculosis or another chronic respiratory condition. Coughs lasting more than two weeks should be investigated — please visit a clinic for evaluation and testing.
conditions.care_level: Clinic (Urgent) / Emergency (if severe breathing difficulty or haemoptysis)

demographic_modifiers.note: Escalate urgency — PMTCT services needed
Escalate — vertically acquired HIV must be identified

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with an immune-related condition or infection. These symptoms warrant a medical evaluation — a clinic can provide confidential testing and support.

demographic_modifiers.note: Highest mortality risk; escalate immediately
Escalate urgency
Use IMCI criteria for breathing rate; fast-track referral

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a severe respiratory infection. Breathing difficulties can worsen quickly — please seek emergency care immediately if your symptoms may be consistent with difficulty breathing at rest.

demographic_modifiers.note: EMERGENCY — immediate isolation and referral regardless of severity
Increase urgency — nosocomial risk

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a serious infectious illness requiring immediate medical evaluation. Please seek emergency care now and inform healthcare staff of your symptoms on arrival.

demographic_modifiers.note: Higher exposure risk — endemic in rural/agricultural areas

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher transmission in rainy season through freshwater contact

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with schistosomiasis or another parasitic condition. Blood in urine should always be investigated — please visit a clinic for testing and treatment.

demographic_modifiers.note: Highest burden; escalate if growth delay or severe anaemia
Severe acute malnutrition — emergency escalation regardless of primary condition severity
Moderate acute malnutrition — increase urgency by one tier

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a parasitic worm infection. This is common and treatable — a pharmacist or clinic can advise on appropriate treatment.

demographic_modifiers.note: Higher exposure risk; escalate immediately — bites often on face/neck

conditions.explanation_template: You may have been exposed to a serious infection through an animal bite. Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis is needed urgently — please go to an emergency facility immediately. Do not wait for symptoms.

demographic_modifiers.note: Very high mortality in third trimester — immediate escalation
EMERGENCY — increase urgency to maximum
Increase urgency — nosocomial risk

seasonal_modifiers.note: Peak transmission November–April; Lassa fever season in Nigeria

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a serious febrile illness. In Nigeria, fever with weakness and sore throat requires urgent medical evaluation — please seek care immediately.

demographic_modifiers.note: Higher risk — MenAfriVac gap

seasonal_modifiers.note: Epidemic season December–June in the Nigerian meningitis belt

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a serious infection affecting the brain or spine. This requires immediate emergency care — please go to hospital now or call for help.

demographic_modifiers.note: Highest risk — DTP vaccination gap
Highest burden age group

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a serious throat infection requiring immediate medical attention. Please seek emergency care now — throat swelling can affect breathing.

demographic_modifiers.note: Significantly increase urgency — vaccination status critical
Higher risk of severe disease

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher mosquito activity; peak transmission risk

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a serious fever-causing illness. Jaundice (yellowing of eyes or skin) with fever requires immediate medical evaluation — please seek emergency care.

demographic_modifiers.note: Increase urgency — higher risk of severe disease
Increase urgency

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with mpox or another rash-causing illness. Please seek medical care and avoid close contact with others — isolation advice will be provided by a healthcare worker.

demographic_modifiers.note: Increase base weight — rising hypertension prevalence in Nigeria
ESCALATE — risk of pre-eclampsia/eclampsia

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with high blood pressure or a related condition. Blood pressure can be measured at a clinic — it is important to have this checked, especially if your symptoms may be consistent with headaches or dizziness.
conditions.care_level: Clinic / Emergency (if stroke or heart attack symptoms)

demographic_modifiers.note: Increase base weight
ESCALATE — gestational diabetes risk
Increase base weight

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with diabetes or a related metabolic condition. These symptoms warrant a blood sugar test — please visit a clinic for assessment and advice.

demographic_modifiers.note: Higher risk of severe attack; escalate with any breathing difficulty
Poorly controlled asthma increases fetal risk; escalate

seasonal_modifiers.note: Dust and dry air triggers exacerbations November–February

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with asthma or a breathing condition. If you use an inhaler, use it now. Seek emergency care immediately if you cannot speak in full sentences or if your lips look blue.

demographic_modifiers.note: Increase base weight
Higher severity risk

seasonal_modifiers.note: Dust triggers exacerbations

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a long-term respiratory condition. A clinic visit is recommended to investigate the cause — chronic cough lasting over two weeks should always be evaluated.

demographic_modifiers.note: ESCALATE — anaemia in pregnancy is a major contributor to maternal mortality
High burden; co-existing malaria/malnutrition common
Severe acute malnutrition — emergency escalation regardless of primary condition severity
Moderate acute malnutrition — increase urgency by one tier

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with anaemia or low blood levels. This is common in Nigeria and has several treatable causes — please visit a clinic for a blood test.

demographic_modifiers.note: Increase urgency — higher cardiovascular risk
Increase urgency
Increase urgency

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a heart or cardiovascular condition. Chest pain — especially with sweating, arm pain, or difficulty breathing — requires emergency evaluation. Please seek immediate care.
conditions.care_level: Clinic / Emergency (if severe chest pain or fainting)

demographic_modifiers.note: Head injury requires immediate assessment
Higher fracture risk from falls

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a minor injury. Most minor injuries can be treated at a pharmacy or clinic. Seek emergency care if there was a head injury, heavy bleeding, or you cannot move the affected area.

demographic_modifiers.note: Scalds common; higher body surface area relative to size — escalate sooner
Escalate for any significant burn

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with a burn injury. Small superficial burns can be treated carefully at home or at a pharmacy. Seek emergency care for large, deep, or facial burns.

demographic_modifiers.note: Higher lethality — smaller body mass; escalate immediately

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher risk during agricultural season and rainy season (Apr–Oct)

conditions.explanation_template: A snake bite is a potential emergency. Please go to an emergency facility immediately — even if the bite seems minor, dangerous venom can act quickly. Do not wait for symptoms to worsen.
conditions.care_level: Emergency (all snake bites should be assessed urgently)

demographic_modifiers.note: Higher fracture and intracranial bleed risk
All road injuries require prompt assessment

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with minor injuries from an accident. Please visit a clinic for assessment — some injuries that seem minor can be more serious. Seek emergency care immediately if there was a head injury or heavy bleeding.

demographic_modifiers.note: Increased risk of pre-eclampsia
ESCALATE — pre-eclampsia risk very high
ESCALATE — gestational diabetes complications

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may indicate a pregnancy-related warning sign. These symptoms require prompt medical attention — please go to a clinic or hospital immediately, especially if there is bleeding or severe headache.

demographic_modifiers.note: All cases are emergency or urgent — neonatal illness deteriorates rapidly
ESCALATE — higher risk of severe infection

conditions.explanation_template: A newborn with fever, poor feeding, or unusual behaviour needs urgent medical attention. Newborn infections can become life-threatening very quickly — please seek emergency care immediately.

demographic_modifiers.note: Core target population — use IMCI breathing rate thresholds (≥50/min <1yr; ≥40/min 1–5yr)
Severe acute malnutrition — emergency escalation regardless of primary condition severity
Moderate acute malnutrition — increase urgency by one tier
Higher risk of PCP pneumonia — escalate urgency

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher incidence November–February due to dry dusty air irritating airways

conditions.explanation_template: Your child's symptoms may be consistent with a respiratory infection or pneumonia. Fast breathing or chest indrawing in a child requires urgent clinic or hospital assessment — please do not wait.

demographic_modifiers.note: Core at-risk group — highest burden
Severe acute malnutrition — emergency escalation regardless of primary condition severity
Moderate acute malnutrition — increase urgency by one tier

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher incidence in lean season before harvest (June–September)

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with malnutrition or inadequate nutritional intake. This condition is treatable — please visit a clinic or health centre for assessment and nutritional support.

demographic_modifiers.note: Severe headache in pregnancy — ESCALATE, rule out pre-eclampsia
Increase urgency — may indicate BP crisis

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms include headache, which is very common and usually not serious. However, a sudden severe headache or headache with fever, stiff neck, or confusion requires urgent medical attention — please seek care promptly.
conditions.care_level: Self-care / Pharmacy (Clinic if persistent or red flags)

demographic_modifiers.note: Escalate for any significant abdominal pain — multiple obstetric causes possible
Escalate with vomiting or fever — appendicitis and intussusception possible

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms include abdominal pain, which has many possible causes. Mild pain may resolve with rest, but persistent or severe pain — especially with fever or vomiting — should be assessed by a healthcare provider.
conditions.care_level: Pharmacy / Clinic (Emergency if severe or red flags)

demographic_modifiers.note: Higher risk of fracture; escalate with post-fall pain
Lower back pain common; escalate if flank pain — rule out UTI

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with musculoskeletal pain or back pain. Most cases are not serious and improve with rest. Seek care if pain is severe, follows an injury, or is accompanied by numbness or weakness.
conditions.care_level: Pharmacy / Clinic (Emergency if neurological signs or post-trauma)

demographic_modifiers.note: Fatigue in pregnancy is common but anaemia must be excluded
Investigate underlying cause — frailty risk

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms include fatigue or weakness, which can have many causes. In Nigeria, malaria and anaemia are common causes. Please see a healthcare provider if fatigue is severe or accompanied by fever or other symptoms.
conditions.care_level: Pharmacy / Clinic (Emergency if sudden or one-sided weakness)

demographic_modifiers.note: Dizziness in pregnancy — rule out anaemia and pre-eclampsia; escalate with headache
Risk of falls; escalate

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms include dizziness, which can have several causes including dehydration, low blood pressure, or anaemia. Most cases are not serious, but seek care if dizziness is severe, causes fainting, or comes with headache or chest pain.
conditions.care_level: Pharmacy / Clinic (Emergency if fainting or neurological signs)

demographic_modifiers.note: Increase urgency — previous reactions may predict severity
Escalate faster — respiratory reserve is lower

seasonal_modifiers.note: Higher incidence of allergic rhinitis

conditions.explanation_template: Your symptoms may be consistent with an allergic reaction. Most mild allergic reactions respond to antihistamines available at a pharmacy. Seek emergency care immediately if your symptoms may be consistent with difficulty breathing, throat swelling, or feel faint.
